info.name: JiggerJot API
info.description:
Complete API surface of the JiggerJot platform (rename per app — see docs/REBRANDING.md).

**Setup**
1. Import `JiggerJot.local.postman_environment.json` and select it.
2. Start the stack: `docker compose up -d` (Postgres + Mailpit) and the API (`dotnet run --project src/Api --launch-profile https`).
3. SMTP must point at **Mailpit** (`localhost:1027`) for the OTP auto-fetch to work — if your `.env` overrides SMTP to a real provider, switch it back for API testing.

**Sign-in flow (folder 1):** `OTP — send` → `OTP — fetch code from Mailpit` (delivery is async; wait ~2–5 s after send) → `OTP — verify`. Tokens are stored in the environment and every request in the collection authenticates with them automatically. Auth requests send `X-Native-Client: true`, selecting the body token transport (no cookies needed in Postman); the refresh token rotates on every `Refresh` call.

**MFA:** if the account has MFA enabled, `OTP — verify` stores a `mfaChallenge` instead of tokens — run `MFA — verify (step-up)` with a TOTP or recovery code.

**Admin folder** needs the signed-in user's email in `Admin__StaffEmails__0` (API restart required). **Public API / Webhooks folders** are config-gated default-off (`PublicApi__Enabled=true`, `Webhooks__Enabled=true`).

request.description: Rate-limited 5/min per IP (429 after — QA-AUTH-11). Email delivery is async (outbox): wait a few seconds before fetching the code.

item.name: OTP — fetch code from Mailpit (local envs only)

request.description: Reads the newest Mailpit message and extracts the 6-digit OTP into {{otpCode}}. Only works in environments with a mailpitUrl (local). On hosted envs (staging/prod) email goes to REAL inboxes — read the code there and set {{otpCode}} manually (or paste it straight into 'OTP — verify').

exec: console.warn('This environment has no Mailpit (hosted env — real email). Read the OTP from your inbox and set {{otpCode}} manually.');
if (!msgs.length) { console.warn('Mailpit is empty — send the OTP first; delivery is async (wait ~2-5s).'); }
else console.warn('No 6-digit code in the newest email — is it the OTP email?');

header.description: Body token transport — refresh_token returned in JSON instead of a cookie (Postman-friendly).

request.description: Stores accessToken/refreshToken on success. If the account has MFA enabled, stores mfaChallenge instead — run 'MFA — verify (step-up)' next. 401 invalid_code = wrong/expired; 401 too_many_attempts = cumulative lockout (QA-AUTH-04); 429 = throttle.

exec: console.log('MFA required — challenge stored. Run: MFA — verify (step-up).');

request.description: Completes sign-in for an MFA-enabled account. Accepts a 6-digit TOTP or a single-use recovery code (case/hyphen/space-insensitive). Challenge is single-use and short-lived (~5 min).

exec: if (json.access_token) { pm.environment.set('accessToken', json.access_token); if (json.refresh_token) pm.environment.set('refreshToken', json.refresh_token); console.log('Step-up complete — tokens stored.'); }

request.description: Rotates the refresh token (old one is revoked; replaying it revokes every session — reuse detection). The stored refreshToken is updated automatically.
The verify half is a browser redirect flow (GET /api/auth/magic-link/verify?token=&email= → 302 to the web app) — click the link from Mailpit in a browser; it isn't meaningful as a pure API call.

**Documentation-only — a browser flow, not runnable from Postman.** Listed so the collection stays a complete mirror of the API surface (v3 audit TR-6; the parity gate `PostmanParityTests` enforces it). Full-page navigation: 302 to the provider's consent screen. {provider} = a configured provider from GET /api/auth/providers. No auth; errors land on the client's /auth-error.

**Documentation-only — a browser flow, not runnable from Postman.** Listed so the collection stays a complete mirror of the API surface (v3 audit TR-6; the parity gate `PostmanParityTests` enforces it). The PROVIDER redirects here after consent (carries its code/state). Issues the session (refresh cookie) and 302s to the client. Never called by an API client directly.

**Documentation-only — a browser flow, not runnable from Postman.** Listed so the collection stays a complete mirror of the API surface (v3 audit TR-6; the parity gate `PostmanParityTests` enforces it). The emailed magic-link URL. Single-use, hashed, time-limited token in the query; consumes it, sets the refresh cookie (or MFA step-up redirect), then 302s to the client.

**Documentation-only — a browser flow, not runnable from Postman.** Listed so the collection stays a complete mirror of the API surface (v3 audit TR-6; the parity gate `PostmanParityTests` enforces it). Opened in the OS browser by MAUI clients (WebAuthenticator). Like /login/{provider} but the callback returns a deep link carrying a one-time code instead of a cookie.

**Documentation-only — a browser flow, not runnable from Postman.** Listed so the collection stays a complete mirror of the API surface (v3 audit TR-6; the parity gate `PostmanParityTests` enforces it). Provider redirect for the native flow: issues a short-lived ONE-TIME CODE and 302s to the app's custom-scheme deep link. The code is redeemed via POST /api/auth/native/exchange.

Redeems the one-time code from the native callback deep link for tokens on the BODY transport (access + refresh token JSON; no cookie). 400/401 invalid_code on unknown/expired/replayed codes (single-use, 5-min TTL); {mfa_required, challenge} when the user has MFA enabled — step up via POST /api/auth/mfa/verify. Requires the X-Native-Client: true header.

en / es shipped. Drives UI + email language. Follows the user across devices: applied (with one reload on mismatch) on every sign-in, and a device-local login-page choice is adopted here automatically on sign-in when unset (PREFS-1, ADR-022). With an impersonation token as bearer → 403 impersonation_not_allowed (server-side guard, v3 ADM-8).

How this reader wants recipe amounts shown (JJ-008). "Metric" or "Imperial", case-insensitive.

**null or omitted clears the preference** back to "never chose", which shows every recipe as its book wrote it. That is a choice a reader can return to, not merely where they start — it is the only way to read the 1930 recipes in the book's own words.

**"Neutral" is rejected with 400.** Neutral is a property of a UNIT, not something a reader can prefer: "show me everything in dashes" is not a request anyone can act on, and accepting it would silently do nothing.

403 from an impersonation session — staff must not mutate the target's preferences (ADR-022). The value comes back on GET /api/auth/me.

light / dark / system (THEME-1 + PREFS-1, ADR-022). All three are stored verbatim and follow the user across devices — "system" means follow the OS scheme; null in the DB means "never chose" (lets sign-in adopt a device-local choice). Lands in the JWT on the next refresh. Anything else → 400 unsupported_theme. With an impersonation token as bearer → 403 impersonation_not_allowed (server-side guard, v3 ADM-8).
Fail-closed: refuses to remove your last sign-in method (QA-SET-05). Link-start (POST /api/auth/link/{provider}) is a browser redirect flow.
GDPR erasure — IRREVERSIBLE. Owner-with-members → 400 (transfer first). Sole owner → 409 until confirm_dissolve=true (which also dissolves the household).

**Documentation-only — a browser flow, not runnable from Postman.** Listed so the collection stays a complete mirror of the API surface (v3 audit TR-6; the parity gate `PostmanParityTests` enforces it). Starts linking an additional OAuth provider to the signed-in account: responds with the provider redirect carrying a short-lived link token; completes at the callback with ?linked=… (or ?link_error=…) on the client's /settings. Requires the Bearer token.

**Documentation-only — a browser flow, not runnable from Postman.** Listed so the collection stays a complete mirror of the API surface (v3 audit TR-6; the parity gate `PostmanParityTests` enforces it). Time-limited signed download URL minted by the export/file surfaces (FILES-2; the token IS the authorization — DataProtection-signed, tenant-scoped). Browser navigation; responds with Content-Disposition: attachment.
Returns the otpauth:// provisioning URI + Base32 secret (shown once). Add the secret to an authenticator app, then Confirm.

exec: if (json.secret) { pm.environment.set('mfaSecret', json.secret); console.log('Secret (add to authenticator):', json.secret); console.log(json.provisioning_uri); }

request.description: Enables MFA and returns the 10 one-time recovery codes (xxxxx-xxxxx) — logged to console, shown ONCE.

exec: if (codes) console.log('RECOVERY CODES (save now, shown once):', codes.join(', '));

request.description: Returns the raw token ONCE (also emailed). 402 = seat quota reached (QA-HH-14). 409 = already a member.

Sign in as the invitee first (re-run folder 1 with the invitee email) — accept joins the CALLER to the inviting household. Errors: 400 invitation_invalid/must_transfer_first/would_abandon_data, 409 already_member, 402 seat_limit_reached when the household downgraded below its reserved seats (BILLING-9 — the token stays pending and works again after an upgrade).
Roles: member | admin (owner is transferred, never assigned). Owner-only.
Owner-only; you become a member afterwards.
Member: leaves + re-homes to a fresh solo household. Owner with members: refused (transfer first). Sole owner: needs confirm_dissolve=true (dissolves).
GDPR export. Returns a signed, time-limited download URL (stored as {{exportDownloadUrl}} — use 'Files — download export'). Metered per plan (402 when the monthly quota is spent).

exec: if (url) { pm.environment.set('exportDownloadUrl', url.startsWith('http') ? url : pm.environment.get('baseUrl') + url); console.log('exportDownloadUrl stored'); }

request.description: The signed URL from the export (GET /api/files/{token}); no bearer needed — the token IS the auth, and it expires.

Clears ALL of the caller's notifications. The scope is REQUIRED (v3 LB-UI-10): read=false = all, read=true = only read; omitting ?read is a 400 (scope_required), so delete-all can never be hit by a dropped param.
Plan, status, seats — owner-only (403 otherwise).
Returns the provider checkout URL (fake provider locally: billing.test/... — won't load, by design).

header.description: The FAKE provider accepts the literal 'valid' (dev only). Real Stripe uses stripe CLI / real signatures.

request.description: Upgrades {{tenantId}} to pro/active as if checkout completed (QA-BILL upgrade loop). Requires the FAKE provider (dev default) — on an environment wired to real Stripe (test mode), this returns 400 invalid signature by design; use `stripe trigger` there instead. Run 'Get household' first to populate {{tenantId}}. Re-sending the same EventId is deduped (inbox); an older OccurredAt than the last applied event is ignored.

item.name: 8 · Admin (platform staff)
item.description: Requires the signed-in user's email in Admin__StaffEmails__0 (repo .env) + API restart. Non-staff → 403 everywhere except 'Am I staff'. An impersonation token ({{impersonationToken}} as bearer) → 403 impersonation_not_allowed on every staff action, and 'Am I staff' reports false — staff powers never transit a sign-in-as session (v3 ADM-2).

exec: if (list.length) { pm.environment.set('adminTenantId', list[0].id); console.log('adminTenantId =', list[0].id, '(' + list[0].name + ')'); }

item.name: Announce to tenant (all members or user_ids subset)

request.description: user_ids: null/omitted = every member; a NON-empty list = just those (intersected with the roster); an explicitly-empty [] = NO ONE (v3 LB-ADM-2). Audited in-tenant.
Queued (202) — the outbox dispatcher fans out a few seconds later. ADR-021.

Simulates a completed checkout (active, never lapses, no provider ids). 409 = tenant has a LIVE Stripe subscription — keyed on liveness (status ≠ canceled), so a churned/canceled tenant is comp-able even though it kept its Stripe id (ADR-006/021, v3 ADM-5).
Deletes the projection (absence ⇒ Free). Idempotent. 409 = LIVE provider subscription (status ≠ canceled); a canceled-but-lingering projection is cleaned up, not blocked (v3 ADM-5).

Stores {{impersonationToken}} (does NOT overwrite your session). To act as the target, temporarily set a request's bearer to {{impersonationToken}}. ~15 min, non-refreshable, audited in the target's tenant.

exec: if (pm.response.code === 200) { pm.environment.set('impersonationToken', pm.response.json().access_token); console.log('impersonationToken stored (expires_in:', pm.response.json().expires_in + 's)'); }

request.description: Staff recovery path (ADR-021 addendum): wipes the user's TOTP secret + recovery codes WITHOUT a code — verify their identity out-of-band first. Also REVOKES the target's refresh tokens/sessions (v3 ADM-7 — compromise recovery). Audited in the target's tenant (admin.mfa.reset) and the user is notified (in-app + email). 204 also when the user had no MFA (idempotent no-op).

item.name: 9 · Public API & keys (config-gated)
item.description: Default OFF — set PublicApi__Enabled=true (repo .env) + restart. Key management is owner-only JWT; /api/public/* authenticates with the key itself.

request.description: Raw pk_ key returned ONCE — stored as {{apiKey}}.

exec: if (json.key) { pm.environment.set('apiKey', json.key); console.log('apiKey stored (shown once):', json.prefix + '…'); }

request.description: Key → tenant-scoped principal. Also accepts Authorization: Bearer pk_… . Per-key rate limit: 60/min → 429.

item.name: 10 · Outbound webhooks (config-gated)
item.description: Default OFF — set Webhooks__Enabled=true (repo .env) + restart. Owner-only. Target URLs must be public-routable (SSRF guard blocks localhost/private ranges) — use https://webhook.site or similar.

request.description: Signing secret (whsec_…) returned ONCE — stored as {{webhookSecret}}. 400 = SSRF guard rejected the URL.

exec: if (json.secret) { pm.environment.set('webhookSecret', json.secret); console.log('webhookSecret stored (shown once)'); }

request.description: Synchronously POSTs a signed test 'ping' and returns { delivered, status_code } (or { delivered:false, error:'delivery_failed' } on a transport error). Records a WebhookDelivery row for the attempt (success and failure), so the Delivery log is populated immediately — run it, then the Delivery log request.

Recent delivery attempts for this subscription (newest first, tenant-scoped): each row has success, status_code, error, event_id. Populated by Send test event (sync) and by published/replayed events (async via the outbox). Captures the newest row's id into {{deliveryId}} for Replay.

Re-enqueues the exact stored payload of {{deliveryId}} (same event id, so a receiver can dedup) → 202; delivered async via the outbox with retry/backoff, which logs its own attempt row. 404 for an unknown or other-tenant delivery id.

item.name: 11 • Cocktail catalog
item.description: Browsing the shared cocktail catalog (CKTL-2). Reads return the seeded catalog PLUS anything the caller's household has added, and never another household's rows — that scoping is the query filter's job, not a parameter here (JJ-031).

query.description: 1-based. Out of range is CLAMPED, not rejected — a read does not 400 over a typo.
Default 20, capped at 100. The cap is what stops one request walking the whole catalog.
Matches anywhere in the name, case-insensitively. Omit to browse everything.

request.description:
Requires a signed-in caller with a household (tenant API policy) → 401 without a token. Returns { items, page, pageSize, total }.

Each item carries name, glass, method, servingType, source, isOwn and ingredientCount. **glass and method may be null** — a quarter of the seeded catalog never stated one, and JJ-034 says null rather than a guess. **source** is load-bearing rather than decoration: four names appear in both source books and one appears twice in the Savoy alone, so two rows are otherwise indistinguishable.

Ordering is by name then id. Name alone is not a total order in this catalog, and a non-total order lets pages overlap.

query.description: One combinable filter on the browse list (FEATURES §11), not a separate view. Absent or false is the whole catalog.

request.description:
Everything this household can make RIGHT NOW, from its shelf.

**Derived at query time, never stored** (JJ-003, JJ-019). There is no is_makeable column and there must never be one: the answer changes the instant a shelf changes or a recipe is edited, and a cached flag would be wrong in between with nothing to say so.

A drink qualifies when every REQUIRED line is satisfied — by the exact ingredient, or by anything the substitution graph allows IN THAT DIRECTION (JJ-004, JJ-006). Optional lines never block (JJ-009); ice and water never appear (JJ-020).

Each result carries `substitutions`: "using Curaçao in place of Cointreau" (FEATURES §9). Empty when the household can pour the drink as written, and empty on an unfiltered browse, where a row makes no makeability claim at all.

Tick a shelf first with the Shelf folder, or this is correctly empty.

query.description: Exactly one required line unsatisfied, after substitutions (FEATURES §10). Absent or false is the whole catalog.
Enable to see the contradiction: nothing is both zero short and one short, so the page comes back empty.

request.description:
Everything this household is EXACTLY ONE required ingredient short of — the shopping driver (FEATURES §10, JJ-019).

Each result names that one bottle in `missingIngredient`. That name is the feature: without it the response is a list of drinks you cannot make, which is most of the catalog.

"One short" is counted AFTER substitutions (JJ-004, JJ-006), so a line the household can cover with something else on its shelf is not missing. A White Lady with gin and Curaçao on the shelf is one LEMON JUICE away, not two ingredients away — and buying Cointreau would be wasted money.

Optional lines never count (JJ-009): an unstocked garnish cannot be the thing you are short of.

Adjacent to `makeable=true` and never overlapping it — zero short is makeable, one short is this. Sending BOTH asks for drinks that are both, and correctly returns an empty page rather than one flag quietly winning.

Rows here still carry `substitutions` (FEATURES §9): buy the missing bottle and you still need to know the rest pours as Curaçao.

Derived at query time, never stored. Tick a partial shelf with the Shelf folder first.

exec: pm.test("every row names the one bottle", () =>

item.name: Cocktails — the bottle that unlocks the most

query.description: How many BOTTLES to rank, 1–25, clamped rather than rejected. It never caps the drinks each bottle names.

request.description:
The almost-makeable set read the other way round (ALMOST-2, **JJ-035**): grouped by the missing ingredient rather than by the cocktail, and ranked.

The request above answers *this drink is missing that bottle*, one drink at a time. On a modest shelf that is eighty-one rows, which is correct and unreadable. This answers *which bottle opens the most, and which drinks* — one sentence someone can act on.

**It runs `almost`'s predicate character-for-character**, so the two readings of the set cannot drift. A test walks both and checks that every drink named here appears in the per-drink list attributed to the same bottle, and that nothing in that list is left out of the ranking.

**`unlocks` always equals the length of `cocktails`.** The card shows the number beside the names, so they are one value read twice rather than two values computed twice — which is why the names are never truncated.

**Ties order by count, then by ingredient name.** Without that second key two bottles that each open three drinks would swap places between requests with nothing behind it, and the card would appear to change its mind.

**An empty shelf ranks nothing** and returns `[]` rather than a guess. Suggesting a first purchase to a household that is one bottle away from *nothing* is a different question with no set to rank — answered by the request below, `GET /api/cocktails/starters`, and deliberately not by this one.

A household's own cocktails count too — same shared-or-tenant filter as everything else (JJ-031). Tick a partial shelf with the Shelf folder first.

item.name: Cocktails — where to start from nothing

query.description: How many bottles to name, 1–25, clamped rather than rejected.

request.description:
Where to start when the shelf is empty (MARGA-3) — the question the request above deliberately does not answer.

**This is not a variant of `/unlocks`.** That one ranks the almost-makeable set, and a household that has ticked nothing is not one bottle away from anything: the set is empty, so there is nothing to rank. This asks a question that needs no shelf at all — *which bottle do these recipes lean on most* — and then removes the ones the household already has.

**`appears` is how many recipes ASK for it, and the copy built on it says exactly that.** An unlocking bottle can promise drinks because it measured them; a starter bottle cannot, since one bottle alone makes very nearly nothing. Reading `appears` as "drinks you could make" would be the one way this endpoint misleads.

**Required lines only** (JJ-009). An optional line never blocks a drink, so an ingredient that only ever garnishes is not one the catalog leans on — counting it would send someone out for a lemon twist.

**Substitutions are ignored**, on purpose: a first bottle should be the one the recipes name, and with an empty shelf there is nothing to substitute from.

**Ties order by count, then by ingredient name**, so the suggestion does not change between requests with nothing behind it. A household's own recipes count towards its own suggestion and never towards anyone else's (JJ-031). Returns `[]` only for a household that already has everything the catalog requires.

exec: pm.test("every suggestion is asked for by something", () =>
body.forEach(b => console.log(b.ingredient + ' is asked for by ' + b.appears + ' recipes'));

request.description:
One cocktail, whole (CKTL-3). {{cocktailId}} is captured by "Cocktails — browse", so run that first.

Every line carries BOTH the authored amount/unit and a `display` string already converted to the caller's PreferredUnitSystem (JJ-007, JJ-008). Converting server-side means one implementation to get right rather than one per client; the authored values are still there for a client that wants to do its own formatting.

Neutral units never convert — a proportional 1930 recipe reads "2/3 part" for every reader, because inventing millilitres for it would state a precision the book never had.

**404, not 403**, for a cocktail belonging to another household: the query filter simply does not return it, and "forbidden" would confirm the row exists.

**Where it stands against your shelf (CKTL-4, FEATURES §12).** `makeability` is `Makeable`, `AlmostMakeable` or `NotMakeable`, and every line carries `availability` (`Have` / `Substitute` / `Missing`) plus `substituteWith` — the bottle you would actually reach for. Sent as names rather than numbers so the wire format survives anyone reordering the enum.

Derived at query time and never stored (JJ-003, JJ-019): tick something in the Shelf folder and this same request answers differently, with nothing to invalidate. It is the same rule the `makeable` and `almost` filters apply, so a drink can never be makeable in the list and not on its own page.

**`forkedFrom`** names the cocktail this one was copied from (FORK-1, JJ-013), or is null. Provenance only — and null again once the original is deleted, because the link is deliberately not a foreign key: the copy survives and simply stops being able to say where it came from.

exec: pm.test("every line is rendered for the reader", () =>
pm.test("every line says how you would pour it", () =>

request.description:
Copies any cocktail this household can see into the household (FORK-1, FEATURES §13). **201** with the new id.

**A snapshot, never a reference** (JJ-002, JJ-013). A new tenant-owned `Cocktail` plus copies of every recipe line, amounts exactly as authored. The shared catalog is read-only and stays that way; the copy is wholly the household's, and later edits to the original never propagate to it.

**`tenant_id` is set by the handler on the cocktail AND on every line.** Nothing stamps either — the interceptor keys off `ITenantScoped` and these tables deliberately are not (JJ-031). A line written without one would land in the shared catalog attached to a household's recipe.

**`forked_from_cocktail_id` is provenance and nothing else**, and deliberately not a foreign key: deleting the original neither blocks nor cascades, and the copy simply stops being able to say where it came from.

**The source credit is NOT copied.** The book wrote the original, not this household's version of it (JJ-032) — carrying it across would attribute whatever the household does next to Craddock or the IBA. Read the fork back with "Cocktails — detail" and compare: `source` is null, `forkedFrom` names the original.

Forking a fork is fine and records the one it came from, not the root. **404** for a cocktail belonging to another household — not 403, which would confirm the row exists.

exec: pm.test("hands back the new id", () => pm.expect(body.id).to.be.a("string"));

request.description:
Everything a household may choose while writing a cocktail (AUTHORING-1, FEATURES §14): glasses, methods, units, serving types and recipe-line roles.

**Not the same list as "Cocktails — filter options", on purpose.** That one is derived from the catalog, so a filter never offers a glass that returns nothing. This one is the whole curated lookup (JJ-022), because someone writing down what they actually pour must be able to reach a glass no seeded recipe happens to use.

Units keep their curated order rather than being alphabetised: it runs from what a person pours most to what they pour least, which is the order a picker wants.

Captures `glassTypeId`, `methodId` and `unitId` for the request below.

body.raw:
{
  "name": "House Negroni",
  "glassTypeId": "{{glassTypeId}}",
  "methodId": "{{methodId}}",
  "servingType": "FullDrink",
  "instructions": "Stir over ice and garnish with orange.",
  "lines": [
    {
      "ingredientId": "{{ingredientId}}",
      "amount": 30,
      "unitId": "{{unitId}}",
      "isRequired": true,
      "role": "Base",
      "notes": null
    }
  ]
}

request.description:
A household writes its own cocktail (AUTHORING-1, FEATURES §14). **201** with the new id.

**It participates in makeable and in filtering immediately**, and that costs nothing: both are derived from the recipe lines at query time (JJ-003, JJ-014), so a drink written a second ago is exactly as visible to the engine as one seeded from a 1930 book. There is no index to rebuild and no tag to remember to set.

`glassTypeId` and `methodId` are **optional** and meant to stay that way (JJ-034): a quarter of the seeded catalog never states a glass. Omit them and the recipe simply does not say.

Line order is the array's — `display_order` is assigned from position, so a client never numbers them. The same ingredient may appear on several lines; there is deliberately no unique index on (cocktail, ingredient), because a split pour is a real thing to write down.

`tenant_id` is set by the handler on the cocktail AND every line (JJ-031, nothing stamps them). No `source_id` and no `forked_from_cocktail_id`: this was written here, not transcribed from a book (JJ-032) and not copied from another recipe (JJ-013).

**Errors, all 400 with a code:** `invalid_name` (blank or over 200), `no_lines` (a cocktail with none would count as *makeable*, since makeability counts unsatisfied REQUIRED lines — it would sit in tonight's list made of nothing), `unknown_ingredient` (a line names something this household cannot see — a reference to an invisible row is how one household learns another exists), `invalid_line` (an amount of zero or less, an unknown unit, or a unit with no amount, which renders as nothing at all and would be a line its author could never see), and `unknown_lookup` (no such glass or method).

Run "Cocktails — authoring lookups" and any ingredient-bearing request first to fill the variables.

exec: pm.test("hands back the new id", () => pm.expect(body.id).to.be.a("string"));
console.log('wrote ' + body.id + ' \u2014 read it back with Cocktails \u2014 detail');

request.description: Substring match, not a prefix match: "martini" finds "Dry Martini". Percent and underscore are escaped, so searching for a literal % searches for a %, not for everything.

exec: pm.test("every hit contains the term", () => body.items.forEach(i => pm.expect(i.name.toLowerCase()).to.include('martini')));

request.description:
What the filter dropdowns offer (FILTER-1, FEATURES §11): methods, glasses and serving types.

Drawn from the cocktails this household can SEE, not from the curated lookup tables. Those hold nineteen glasses and ten methods and any given catalog uses a fraction of them — a filter whose options mostly return nothing reads as broken rather than as precise. It also means the lists grow by themselves when the full 969-recipe catalog is switched on, and that a household's own cocktails contribute their glasses while another household's never do.

Captures `methodId` and `glassId` for the next request.

query.description: Matched against the ingredient's NAME, its CATEGORY and its SUBCATEGORY at once, so a parent catches every child (JJ-015, JJ-016).
Shot or FullDrink, case-insensitive. Anything else is treated as no filter rather than a 400.

request.description:
Exploring the catalog rather than searching it (FILTER-1, FEATURES §11). Every parameter here combines — with each other, with `search`, and with the `makeable` and `almost` toggles. Enable the disabled ones above to see it: each is an AND, never a last-one-wins.

**`ingredient` is read off the recipe lines**, because there is no "main spirit" column and there never will be — a drink with two spirits or none makes that field a lie (JJ-014). The text is compared against the ingredient's name, its category and its subcategory at once: "rum" finds the dark and the white, "dark rum" finds only the dark, and "elderflower" finds a thing no editor would have thought to tag.

`method` and `glass` take ids from "Cocktails — filter options". A recipe that never stated a glass (JJ-034) does not match a glass filter: no glass is not a glass.

An id nobody recognises matches nothing and returns an empty page — a read with a bad id is a caller's typo, not a reason to hand back a 400. Wildcards in `ingredient` are escaped, so `%` looks for a percent sign rather than returning the whole catalog and looking for all the world like a working filter.

item.name: 12 • Shelf (inventory)
item.description: What a household has on its shelf (INV) — the checklist "what can I make right now" reads. Ordinary tenant-scoped data: the platform's global filter, write stamping and RLS policy all apply, so nothing here re-spells tenancy.

request.description:
The WHOLE catalog this household can see — shared plus its own — each row carrying `isAvailable`. The full list rather than only what is ticked, because you cannot tick what you cannot see, and absence of an inventory row is exactly what "not available" means (JJ-023).

Every row carries its `category` so each client groups the same way; 191 ingredients is far too many to tick down a flat list.

Ice and water are absent by construction — always available, never modelled as blocking inventory (JJ-020).

Ticks or unticks one ingredient → 204. {{ingredientId}} is captured by "Shelf — list", so run that first.

Unticking UPDATES the row rather than deleting it: "I checked and I do not have it" is worth keeping apart from "I never looked", and everything that reads the shelf filters on `isAvailable` so absence and false behave identically.

**404, not 403**, for an ingredient this household cannot see. A different answer would let someone probe ids to discover another household's custom ingredients.

item.name: Shelf — set many at once (the wizard's write)

request.description:
A whole shelf in one request (ONBOARD-1, FEATURES §7 — *optimized for fast bulk-checking*).

**Deliberately not the same shape as the request above.** On the shelf screen a tick is a decision someone just made and should be saved before they look away, which is why that one writes a single ingredient and the UI rolls back if it fails. The wizard is the opposite: it puts a dozen suggestions on screen **already ticked** and asks which are wrong, so nothing is confirmed until Finish. Writing as it went would record a shelf the household never confirmed, and leave half of one behind for anyone who closed the tab midway.

**The state is stated, never toggled.** Each entry says what that ingredient should BE, so the result does not depend on what the shelf happened to hold when the request landed — and sending the same body twice leaves the same shelf rather than a second row per ingredient, which matters because a wizard finishing on a flaky connection is exactly what produces a retry.

**Always 200.** An id this household cannot see comes back in `unknown` rather than failing the request: the catalog can change under a wizard that has been open a while, and losing eleven good ticks because the twelfth went stale is the wrong trade. That same filter is the authorization check — another household's custom ingredient simply is not visible, so it lands in `unknown` like any unrecognised id.

**Unticking updates the row rather than deleting it** (INV-1, JJ-023), the same as the single-ingredient write.

Run *Shelf — list* first to pick a real `ingredientId`.

The two-level ingredient category tree, for the picker on the add form (JJ-015): top-level categories, each with its subcategories.

Curated and global — no household additions in MVP (JJ-022) — so this is a read and will stay one. Filtering a parent matches all its children (JJ-016), which is why the pairing matters and why the add below rejects a subcategory belonging to some other category.

Captures `categoryId` and `subcategoryId` for the next request.

The bottle the catalog has never heard of (INV-2, FEATURES §8). Creates a **tenant-owned** `Ingredient` and ticks it, so it comes back ready to pour: someone adds a bottle to their shelf because it is on their shelf, and making them add it and then tick it is two actions for one intent. It unticks like any other row.

**`tenant_id` is set by the handler, by hand.** Nothing stamps it — the stamping interceptor keys off `ITenantScoped` and this table deliberately is not (JJ-031). A row written without it would land in the SHARED catalog, visible to every household; the RLS insert policy would refuse the attempt, which is the backstop doing its job.

**A household ingredient satisfies a recipe line by exact name only** and never joins the substitution graph, whose ends must both be shared rows (JJ-005, JJ-018).

**409 `ingredient_exists`** when the name is already visible to this household — its own or the shared catalog's, compared case-insensitively — carrying `existingIngredientId` so a client can offer to tick that instead. The unique index alone does not catch the second case: it is keyed on (tenant_id, name), so your "campari" and the catalog's "Campari" are different rows to the database.

**400 `invalid_name`** for a blank name, **400 `invalid_category`** for an unknown category, a subcategory passed where a category belongs (the tree is two levels, JJ-015), or a subcategory belonging to a different parent.

Send `subcategoryId` as an empty string or omit it to file the ingredient at the top level.
